persons.name: Sarah
persons.harm: Over a roughly eight-month relationship and engagement (Sept 2017 to May 2018) her fiance love-bombed, gaslit and isolated her, controlled money, and impersonated a fake married couple ('Kimmy and Brian') by text for months to manipulate and body-shame her and turn her against her parents. He also abused her dog. After the breakup he tried to log into her accounts and used her old credit card.
persons.outcome_quote: Looking back, I would not change a damn thing. I think he saved my life.
persons.notes: The relationship ended because her parents formally asked her to postpone the wedding, she uncovered the fake 'Kimmy' herself with her roommates, and her family organised the move-out; no institution ended it. A cousin who is a police officer watched the ex's house during the move-out, but he did so as a relative and no report was made, so it is not coded as a contact. She repeatedly said she would go to police or file a restraining order or an animal-abuse report if he did anything more (s1-e9 @ 6:17, @ 26:13, @ 32:24; s1-e10 @ 65:37), but none was filed. A vet saw injuries consistent with a kick on her rehomed dog (s1-e3-maple-finn @ 11:34); that is about the animal, so it is not coded as a contact. The show says everything was fact-checked and cites a paper trail and vet visits (s1-e9 @ 51:55). Her counseling and church community supported her recovery.

coder_notes: All 8 chunk files read in full. Season 1 = Something Was Wrong (Sarah). The perpetrator is called by a show pseudonym, written as [perpetrator] in quotes. Only Sarah's harm reached institutions, and only peripherally (bank, airline, counselor); no police, court or protective action for her is reported, and nobody reported the perpetrator to any authority. The season ends with no conviction or charge. Animals (Sarah's dog Maple, his dog Finn) are not person records; a vet's finding of possible kick injury is noted under Sarah. Sarah's family were deceived but are not coded as harmed persons. 'T' (the season 2 subject) appears at the live show, but her story belongs to season 2 and is not coded. The expert episode (s1-e15, therapist Isaac Smith) contains no personal stories. Several listener and aside stories are thin and coded with low confidence. Allison's outcome is not stated, so not_protected is a forced choice.
